executiveSummary: This period saw multiple high-urgency incidents driven by generative AI and synthetic media. Microsoft and partners disrupted the EvilTokens phishing-as-a-service operation, linked to the compromise of more than 12,000 Microsoft accounts across over 10,000 organizations and arrests in the UK, underscoring how AI-assisted tooling is scaling business email compromise and fraud campaigns View Article View Article . Prosecutors in New York also seized 12 domains involved in AI-generated non-consensual sexual imagery affecting over 1,200 victims, highlighting persistent harms from deepfake exploitation View Article . Election integrity featured prominently: Brazil's top electoral court acted following the use of AI-generated political endorsement imagery Source , while CISA released a U.S. election security plan addressing ongoing cyber and influence risks around voter databases and patching View Article . A U.S. proposal for bilateral AI incident alerts with China indicates elevated national-security concern over destabilizing AI events View Article . Additional escalations included a reported criminal appeal in New Mexico that allegedly contained fabricated AI-generated police testimony-raising acute due-process risks Source -and active fraud schemes spoofing FBI complaints using AI-generated video to harvest personal and financial data Source . Defensive and governance developments included NIST media-forensics evaluation work, a European transparency code for labeling deepfakes, and research on hijacking AI browser agents via malicious extensions View Article View Article View Article . Overall, given the scale of AI-assisted phishing, ongoing deepfake exploitation, and election-related incidents, the near-term threat environment appears to be worsening.
